notes:
I don't have any notes on Daniel 12 to give you yet. My first attempt to read the commentary pages failed, and the tool limit stopped me before I could retry or read any content. Your rules say to report only what the pages say and never fill gaps from memory, so I haven't written anything.

These are the pages I tried to read. The download attempt finished, but I never got to see whether each page actually loaded:
- Enduring Word (David Guzik): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/daniel-12/
- Ellicott: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/daniel/12.htm
- Pulpit Commentary: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/daniel/12.htm
- Gill: https://biblehub.com/commentaries/gill/daniel/12.htm
- Precept Austin: https://www.preceptaustin.org/daniel-12-commentary
- NET Bible notes: https://netbible.org/bible/Daniel+12

If you send another message, I'll start again with this plan:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** the six pages above, plus Matthew Henry and Barnes on studylight.org or biblehub.com.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly v. 1 (who Michael is, and when the time of distress comes), v. 2 (bodily resurrection), v. 4 (what "knowledge will increase" means) and vv. 7, 11–12 (the "time, times, and half a time" and the 1,290 and 1,335 days). For these I'd read the traditions' own teachers: gty.org and desiringgod.org (Baptist), ligonier.org and thegospelcoalition.org (Reformed), wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), lcms.org and 1517.org (Lutheran), enduringword.com and ag.org (Pentecostal), and gotquestions.org.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes and bibleodyssey.org for modern scholarship. For Catholic and Orthodox readings, newadvent.org (Jerome's Daniel commentary and the Catholic Encyclopedia), catholic.com and oca.org.

I'll put each point under its verse with the page it came from, and leave out anything I can't find.
